title: Metric counter flash ticks
prompt: Output: one WAV, 48 kHz / 16-bit / stereo, exactly 144,000 samples (3.0 s at 30 fps = 90 frames). Python + numpy/scipy only. Synthesise everything (no samples, no downloads, no speech). Fixed random seed (np.random.default_rng(55)). A 3-second counting-up metric flash for dashboards and ad promos. Frames 0-60: a numeric counter ticks: clean digital clicks (1 ms 5 kHz sine burst + tiny noise transient) starting at 6/s and accelerating to 30/s, with pitch rising from B5 to F#7 in B minor scale steps every 6 ticks. Under it a faint sine riser B3→B4. Frame 60: the number locks: a bright two-layer 'ding' (FM bell B6 + glass partial at F#7, 600 ms decay) plus a soft sub tap on B1 and a 30 ms white-noise sparkle, panned centre; frames 60-90: light stereo shimmer tail (short ping-pong 125 ms delay). Silence from frame 84 to the end apart from the decaying tail. Master: -14 LUFS integrated, true peak <= -1 dBTP (4x oversampled peak check), last frames fade to exactly 0. You can't listen, so verify: measure loudness and true peak with ffmpeg ebur128 (peak=true), check the exact sample count, confirm the energy change lands on each cue frame, check every note fits the chord under it, render a spectrogram PNG and inspect it. Fix and re-render until every check passes, then report the numbers.
notes: Accelerating digital counter ticks rising in B minor into a glass ding lock at frame 60 with shimmer tail.
